_about: Complete release history, structured for the planned in-plugin 'What's New' viewer. CHANGELOG.md stays the human-readable copy; this file is the machine-readable one. Keep both in step when cutting a release. Newest release first. 'change.type' is one of: new, changed, fixed, removed, internal. 'published' is false for versions that exist in the repo's history but were never served from repo.json, so a viewer can skip them or fold them into the release that shipped their features.

releases.headline: Ratings are retired, and the Party Finder gets a board, a Join button and coordinated parties
releases.notes: Ratings are gone on the server too: POST /ratings answers 403 ratings_retired so an older build in the wild drops its queue rather than retrying, and the duty allowance behind the post-duty window is frozen rather than computed. Progression, clears and the feed are untouched. The new backend work - the board, coordination, feedback, portraits, fight art and the clears stream - lives in the backend repository.

changes.title: Ratings are retired
changes.body: Nobody can vote on anybody any more, no score is shown anywhere, and the window that appeared the moment you left a duty is gone. Nothing replaces it. The Players tab keeps search, profiles, clears and everyone you have met, and the community half of the plugin is progression, clears and the feed. The server is part of this too: the vote endpoint now answers 403 ratings_retired, so an older build drops the votes it was holding instead of asking again every few minutes for the rest of its life.

changes.title: A leader's score is no longer printed on a listing
changes.body: The community score that used to appear beside the leader's name on the game's own listing window is removed, and the setting that controlled it is gone from Settings. The board card shows loot rule, item level, tags, time left and seats instead.

changes.title: A Party Finder tab
changes.body: A new tab lists every recruitment listing any plugin user's Party Finder window has been handed, for a region and data centre you pick - your own first, then the others. Cards or one line per listing, search across duty, leader, comment, data centre and member names, fifty a page with a range. It is recruitment notices only: what the game's own window shows anybody on that data centre, and nothing about who is in a party unless somebody in it is running the plugin. It is there on a fresh install and needs no setting to read.

changes.title: A Join button on every listing on your data centre
changes.body: Press Join and the plugin opens the listing, which makes the game fetch it afresh, puts that fresh copy on the board so the card shows exactly what the game shows, checks it, and only then presses Join Party. What it checks, in the order the game itself would object: private without a password, no open seat, wrong world, duty level, duty not unlocked, item level, completion requirement, no open seat that takes your job, one player per job, and whether the game is offering Join Party at all. A refusal is one sentence on the card and the same sentence in chat. Shown only for your own data centre, because anywhere else is a data centre travel, which is what Apply is for.

changes.title: Alliance raids get a Join per party
changes.body: A 24-man listing shows each party and its seats, with a Join for each one. Pressing one with no party specified picks the first party with a seat that fits you.

changes.title: Apply, and hand the party over
changes.body: Plugin parties take applications from other data centres. Press Apply and you are registered and nothing else - you stay free until the listing is full, and every open seat has an applicant. Then the host's plugin takes the public listing down, reposts it privately with a random four-digit password, and each applicant is asked to accept. Nothing moves your character before you accept. Once you do, the plugin travels to the host's data centre if it has to, waits until you have arrived, and joins. If the listing stops being full your offer is withdrawn and you keep your place in the queue. A seat is held by job, so if nothing on the listing fits the job you applied with you are turned away with that said plainly. You can also press Join party now to go straight in without waiting for the party to fill.

changes.title: Refresh on your own data centre reads the game
changes.body: On the data centre you are standing on, the board's refresh button opens the Party Finder, reads every page with the window kept off-screen, and makes the board exactly what it shows. A listing that has gone comes off, one that changed is updated. Anywhere else, or while your character is busy, it fetches the board as it stands. Rate-limited to one game read every five minutes.

changes.title: The plugin reads the Party Finder while you are away
changes.body: The board only knew a listing when somebody's window had been handed it, so a data centre nobody was browsing emptied out and a listing its owner had refreshed still disappeared at its old time. So on a schedule the plugin opens the list itself, lets the game download every page, and closes it again, with the window transparent and off-screen and its real position put back afterwards. It only starts after fifteen seconds with no mouse or keyboard input and stops the instant you touch anything, and never in an instance, in combat, or over any other Party Finder action. Off by default: turn on "Share my party finder data actively" to read every ten minutes whether or not you are at the keyboard. Your own browsing counts as a read - open the list on the Data Centre tab with every category showing and page to the end, and the board is tidied to match.

changes.title: Your own listing reports itself
changes.body: The recruiter's own plugin now says so, the moment a listing goes up, whenever somebody joins or leaves, whenever it is re-posted, and once more as a withdrawal when it comes down. So your listing reaches the board even on a data centre nobody else is browsing, and appears when you post it rather than the next time somebody happens to browse.

changes.title: Auto Refresh runs off your listing's own clock
changes.body: The old refresher counted a number of minutes and fired, whatever the listing said - so a listing re-posted by hand in the meantime was refreshed again for nothing, and a refresh that silently failed was not noticed until the listing had expired. It now reads your listing's clock, waits until exactly the threshold, refreshes, and reads the clock again thirty seconds later. Above the threshold means the refresh took; still at or under means it did not, and it tries again. Nothing moves on to waiting until a refresh is seen to have worked. The footer says whether it is checking, refreshing, or holding a refresh up and why - "due - Party Finder open", "due - in combat". The setting is "Refresh at N min left", 3 to 55, and an install that had the old fixed interval keeps the same schedule: "every 20 minutes" and "at 40 minutes left" are the same thing on a fresh listing.

changes.title: A Feedback tab
changes.body: Report a bug, ask for something, or just say something. Four categories, a message box that counts, and an optional name for the author to reach you by in game. It goes to the author's Discord through the server, so the webhook address never ships in the plugin and the server stores your message first, which means a Discord outage delays it rather than losing it. The tab is there whether or not you are taking part in the community, because a bug report is not a community feature.

changes.title: A watched listing in its own window
changes.body: Watch any listing and it floats into a small window with the duty, the leader, the data centre, the time left and the seats filling. A lock stops it being dragged, and a listing that is re-posted stays the same watch, because it is followed by leader.

changes.title: Dancing Mad says which mechanic a member is on
changes.body: For that duty only, and on a switch under the list, each party member's progress grows a mechanic name - "P4 58% - Grand Cross 3 - Kefka Says" - taken from the phase and boss HP of their furthest logged pull. Approximate on purpose: gear, uptime, deaths and Limit Breaks move the ranges, and the hover says so.

changes.title: A new look throughout
changes.body: Line icons instead of solid ones, iOS system colours, party rows as rounded cards with bare job icons, and settings rebuilt as one row per setting: name in white, a round explanation button, control on the right, a hairline between. The controls are new - a switch with an overshoot, a stepper pill, a dropdown menu, segmented pills, circular colour swatches. The list of settings pages has become a sidebar on a wide window and a bottom bar on a narrow one, and there is one page at a time. Party Finder role tiles are now read out of the game's own texture rather than redrawn. The type scale and the corner radii did not change.

changes.title: A member is described by the job they joined on
changes.body: A Party Finder seat is taken on a job and the listing keeps saying that job, whatever its holder switches to afterwards - a healer who wanders off to craft is still the healer as far as the listing is concerned. Everything the plugin says about a listing to other players now says the job joined on, not the job worn right now. A healer who switched to a crafter for the walk back was being published as a crafter, so the listing's seats and the coordination's seating mis-described a party the game's own window still called SCH.

changes.title: Clears are pushed, not polled
changes.body: The announcer used to learn about a clear by reading the feed on a two-minute grid, so a clear reached people anywhere up to two minutes after it happened and every client asked every two minutes whether anything had. The server now writes each new clear to every connected client at once, so everybody hears it in the same second and a quiet evening costs one ping every twenty-five seconds. The poll is still there as a fallback, so the worst case is the old behaviour and never silence. A reconnect waits a random two to thirty seconds, so a server restart does not bring every client back at once.

changes.title: Old progress says it is old
changes.body: A reading from over a day ago is greyed, says when it is from, and says how to get a current one. Somebody progging moves a phase in an evening, so yesterday's reading is a claim about who they were rather than who they are. Progress now sits in a tinted pill, and people who have opted out or are hidden no longer get a Fetch button that cannot work.

changes.title: Your party list shows every seat while a listing is up
changes.body: The seats nobody is in are there too, waiting, in italics with a light sweeping through them, and the ones you omitted read Omitted. Only while a listing is up - yours, or the one you joined.

changes.title: The community section is called the community
changes.body: "Enable ratings system" is "Take part in the community", "Show ratings on your party" is "Show your party's progress", and the confirmations say what is actually sent: who you finished a duty with, and clears worth posting to the feed.

changes.title: The sharing switch is no longer hidden
changes.body: It used to be drawn only while "Show listing details" was on. Publishing runs on its own now, so turning the panel off would have hidden the switch while the party went on being published - and a setting somebody cannot see is one they cannot turn off either.

changes.title: A member whose game lost the leader's listing still sees the duty
changes.body: The game keeps one listing at a time and drops the leader's the moment another is looked at, or never had it for somebody who joined through a link or an invite. The duty, the seats and the comment come off the board instead. Without that a member saw no duty, and with no duty no progress column at all.

changes.title: A listing could lose its healer and gain a fifth DPS
changes.body: Three separate ways. Posting a listing with people already in the party seated them by position, so a Black Mage took the pure-healer seat and every refresh after kept it that way - members are now seated by the job the seat takes, in the order the game seats them. The slot adjuster guessed the role of a vacated seat from whoever had been sitting in it, so a healer who left had their seat become DPS; a vacated seat now goes back to what the plugin posted it as, and only vacant seats are ever touched. And the coordination's own verification rebuilt a listing's seats from a reading, which is how a listing's real seats were once replaced. Auto-adjust also no longer re-opens the seats your preset deliberately closed.

changes.title: A full party stayed on the board as 8/8
changes.body: The game takes a listing down when the last seat fills, but the client reporting it could go on believing it was in a party. A party of eight is full and a full party is not recruiting, so it is taken down instead - and the same goes for a light party at four, or a listing with seats omitted once the rest are taken.

changes.title: Stepping away from the keyboard looked like you had stopped recruiting
changes.body: A character shows one status, the highest-ranked of those set, and Away from Keyboard, Busy, In Duty and Viewing Cutscene all outrank Recruiting. Reading the displayed one decided that a host who stepped away had stopped recruiting - the exact moment a listing most needs looking after. Every status that is set is read now, not the one on display. The same misreading hid other people's recruitment from you, which said nothing either way when it could not tell; a leader whose statuses cannot be read is now recorded as unknown rather than as not recruiting.

changes.title: The page-forward arrow stopped working on page two
changes.body: A button carries a chain of events - mouse over, mouse out, click - and the first is not always the click. Forward turned page one fine; on page two the same call fired something else and the page never moved.

changes.title: A clear banner drew over other windows but was behind them for clicks
changes.body: Painting on the foreground list puts the banner over everything, but the mouse goes to whichever window is on top - and the banner takes no focus when it appears, so any window focused after it sat above it and got every click while the banner drew over them looking clickable. It is raised in the display order every frame now, so the hit target matches what is on screen. Display order only: keyboard focus stays where you left it.

changes.title: A search box's cross could not be pressed
changes.body: It was an invisible button laid over the field, and it could not be pressed while the field had focus - which is always, since you have just been typing in it. ImGui gives every click inside an active widget to that widget, so the press moved the caret instead. The mouse is now read against the rectangle directly.

changes.title: A listing of somebody else's was kept in view less often than it should be
changes.body: Only a listing's owner can read their own listing, so the only way another party's arrives is when you open its detail window. The watcher now opens the game's window only when there is something to find, and compares once a frame when the card is off-screen and once a second when it is on, rather than the other way round.

changes.title: The server could refuse a session fifty times a minute
changes.body: After a refused session every caller asked again on every attempt, which kept a rate limit permanently hit and could keep it hit for an hour. Nobody asks again until the server's Retry-After, minimum ten seconds. The twenty-second retry loop for a broken connection is bounded too, and a malformed answer is not retried at all.

changes.title: Your own listing's seats were read from the wrong place
changes.body: They were read from the recruitment window's memory, which is the last recruitment set up on this client and stops describing the live listing after a relog - it read as eight seats of any job, and a repost built from it replaced a listing's real seats with that.

changes.title: A refresh held up by the Party Finder waited a full minute every time
changes.body: It was asking a condition flag that stays set for as long as the listing is up, window or no window, so every due refresh was held for the full minute and the countdown looped. The windows are what you would actually lose, and a read never holds a refresh up at all - the game itself can leave the Party Finder open after one, which would otherwise have stalled the check behind it for as long as nobody closed it.

changes.title: A status box sized itself a line short when a comment had a line break in it
changes.body: The whole comment was wrapped as one run, so a line break the author typed counted as one line while the drawing honoured the break and drew two, and every panel sized from the count came out short. Each paragraph is wrapped on its own.

changes.title: The "Read the update" button in Settings did nothing
changes.body: A sheet only appears once it is opened as one, and setting the flag alone left the button doing nothing at all.

changes.title: A share code had no visible line breaks
changes.body: It has no spaces, so it drew as one unbroken run across the window. Export draws it hard-wrapped and read-only, import hides the raw text while you are not typing in it and draws it wrapped underneath, and there is a From clipboard button beside Import.

changes.title: Applicants were reported as a job they had switched away from
changes.body: See "A member is described by the job they joined on" above.

changes.title: One step removed from the first run
changes.body: The voting step is gone from the setup screen and from the tour, and a fresh install lands on Settings rather than Recruit.

releases.headline: Everyone's vote counts once, and Clears loads as you scroll
releases.notes: The vote change is server-side as well as client-side: existing scores were rebuilt so that every voter counts once. The migrations behind that live in the backend repository.

changes.title: Everyone's vote on you counts once
changes.body: Rating the same person again used to stack another vote on top of the last one, worth a tenth but still another one, so a group who play together every week piled up hundreds between them - a score of +300 could be eight people rather than three hundred. Your vote is now a position rather than a tally: upvote somebody and you have upvoted them, however many times you press it.

changes.title: You can change your mind whenever you like
changes.body: Downvoting somebody you upvoted moves your one vote across instead of adding to it, and there is no longer a day to wait out before you can. The button used to grey itself out for twenty-four hours, which made changing your mind impossible rather than merely slow. What counts is the last thing you said.

changes.title: Every vote is worth the same
changes.body: An upvote is +1 and a downvote is -1, from anybody: no more half a vote from a friend or a quarter from an account with no history. A vote either counts in full or it is held until the account has earned its place, and holding is what stopped fake votes in the first place - a quarter of a vote still moved a score.

changes.title: Existing scores were rebuilt to match
changes.body: Almost everybody's percentage is unchanged. The totals came down because the duplicates went, not because anybody's opinion changed.

changes.title: Clears loads as you scroll
changes.body: Sixteen at a time, with the next sixteen fetched as you approach the bottom, instead of numbered pages. It also remembers where you were when you come back to the tab.

changes.title: New clears no longer shove the list around
changes.body: A clear arriving while you are reading used to move everything under your cursor. A button floats at the top of the list instead, and pressing it takes you to the newest.

changes.title: My clears
changes.body: Clears has two tabs: Broadcast, the feed of everybody's clears as before, and My clears, every clear of your own that has gone up on it. My clears appears with your first clear and is not there before that.

changes.title: Removed the divider above "Recent clears"
changes.body: It drew a line between the tab's own header and the first thing inside the tab, which is not a boundary that needed marking.

releases.headline: Listing rosters, a party list that works on your own, and progression that stays put

changes.title: The listing panel shows who is in the party
changes.body: The panel beside a party finder listing now lists who is already in that party. One person in the party running the plugin is enough to describe the whole of it, so a listing is legible even when nobody else in it uses this. Only a publicly listed party is ever published, it is withdrawn when the listing ends, and the setting is under Settings -> PF Radar.

changes.title: Your own row while recruiting alone
changes.body: A listing posted with nobody in it yet now shows you, with your progression and a way to fetch it. The party list previously drew nothing at all until the first person joined, which is the one moment the information was worth having.

changes.title: Progression no longer disappears
changes.body: Prog points would drop back to "Fetch" while the server held the answer, most often with a listing open beside your own party list. The two panels shared one store and overwrote each other's results; each fight and character now has its own entry, so every surface shows the same answer at the same time.

changes.title: Update progress no longer swallows a press
changes.body: A press landing while the plugin was already reading was refused in silence, leaving a button that looked broken. Reads no longer block each other, and a press that genuinely cannot go through now says so.

changes.title: Omitted slots stay omitted
changes.body: Omitting a slot held until the first person left the party, at which point the locked-slot adjuster read every closed seat as a free one and recruited for the roles you had struck off. Closed seats are now left alone.

changes.title: Omitted slots are posted where the game puts them
changes.body: Omitted slots are now moved to the end of the listing before it is posted, which is the shape the game settles a listing into anyway. The roles you kept keep their order and slide up into the gaps.

changes.title: The "Read the update" button
changes.body: Removed from Settings -> About, along with the post it opened.

releases.headline: Two layouts, an overhauled UI, and duty spoiler locking

changes.title: Portrait and landscape layouts
changes.body: The window now comes in two fixed shapes: portrait, one column with a tab bar along the bottom, and landscape, wider with a sidebar and two-column pages. Neither can be resized - each is drawn for the size it is. Pick one in Settings under Appearance.

changes.title: Overhauled UI across the plugin
changes.body: New fonts, resized icons and buttons, and rounded corners throughout. Every prompt is now drawn inside the window rather than as a second window beside it, and confirmations are small centred alerts rather than full-width panels.

changes.title: Spoiler setting for unlocked duties
changes.body: A setting in Party Finder hides and locks any duty the current character has not unlocked, and stops such a preset being applied. Leave it off to see the duty names with locked ones marked, or turn it on to keep unseen content out of the picker entirely.

changes.title: Role slots default to a real composition
changes.body: With auto-select jobs off, slots used to be left free-for-all. Every category now has a default: a light party is a tank, a healer and two of anything that does damage, and an eight-player duty is two of each and four damage. A preset also carries only as many seats as its content fields.

changes.title: Clears notify on each new clear
changes.body: The Clears tab marks itself when somebody posts a clear you have not seen. Hearts are locked to the character that cast them and can be taken back by pressing again.

changes.title: The PF Analysis button steps aside
changes.body: It hides while the game's own recruitment criteria window or a listing's details are open, so the plugin is not offering a second button over a window that has already asked you something.

changes.title: FATEs and The Hunt stay on your world
changes.body: Both force "limit recruiting to my world" on, because neither survives the trip from another world, and your previous setting is restored when you pick a different category.

changes.title: Some duty categories are unavailable for now
changes.body: Duty Roulette, PvP, Gold Saucer, FATEs, Treasure Hunt and Deep Dungeons cannot currently be posted with the correct duty, so they are hidden rather than putting up a listing that says the wrong thing. Presets for them are kept and will return with the category.

changes.title: Presets saved without pressing Save
changes.body: Opening New preset created and saved the preset immediately. It is now only kept when Save is pressed.

changes.title: Dungeons were sized as a full party
changes.body: Light-party content now recruits four seats rather than eight.

changes.title: Omit did not omit the slot
changes.body: Omitting a role in the job selector had no effect while auto-adjust roles was on, which was the default for a new preset. Auto-adjust is now offered only where the game supports it, and the slot editor is yours everywhere else.

changes.title: Language letters were not centred
changes.body: J, E, D and F sat against the left edge of their buttons.

releases.headline: Downvoting fixed; ratings on by default

changes.title: Downvoting always failed with 'That rating couldn't be sent'
changes.body: A score validation check that was meant to block invalid values was also rejecting -1, the value a downvote sends. Upvoting was unaffected. The check now correctly accepts +1 and -1 only.

changes.title: Community ratings on by default for new installs
changes.body: The rating system master switch, the post-duty prompt, and ratings on the party panel all default to enabled. Existing installs keep whatever they had set.

changes.title: Apply was available while queued or in a duty
changes.body: The Apply button stayed green while you were sitting in the Duty Finder queue, and posting a listing from there drops your queue registration. It is now disabled - with the reason on hover - for the Duty Finder queue (including a popped duty awaiting acceptance) and while inside a duty.

changes.title: Presets half-applied from the World or Private tab
changes.body: The Party Finder remembers which of its three search-area tabs (Data Centre, World, Private) was last used, but recruitment can only be set up from Data Centre. Starting from either of the others broke the setup sequence partway. Applying a preset now forces the tab back to Data Centre first, whether or not the window is already open.

changes.title: Auto-Adjust Roles is on by default for new presets
changes.body: Mirrors the in-game 'Seek Job Distributions' option. It is what most listings want and it fills around whoever is already in your party. Only newly created presets are affected - saved presets keep whatever they were set to, since the field has always been serialised.

releases.headline: Preset sharing, macro support, and a refresher you can actually tune
releases.notes: Ships the 3.0.0 features as well - 3.0.0 was never served from the plugin repo, so users upgrade straight from 2.1.2 to this.

changes.title: Share presets with a one-line code
changes.body: Pick Share on any preset's menu and you get a single line of text with a copy button - paste it in Discord and anyone running PF Presets can use your setup. The Import button next to Create New Preset takes one back in, either pasted into the box or pulled straight off your clipboard. Codes that aren't PF Presets codes, or that got cut off mid-copy, are rejected with a plain explanation instead of importing something broken.

changes.title: /pfp apply <name>
changes.body: Posts a preset without opening the window, so a preset can live on a hotbar macro. Partial names work as long as they're unambiguous. Added /pfp list to see the exact names.

changes.title: Auto Refresher is no longer locked to 15 or 30 minutes
changes.body: Double-click the interval to type any value from 1 to 55. Next to it there's a new Stop after limit - set it and the refresher stops renewing your listing after that many hours, so a Party Finder can't sit up all night unattended. Your listing isn't cancelled when the limit hits; it just expires the way it normally would. 'Never' (the default) keeps the old behaviour.

changes.title: A renamed duty could post the wrong listing
changes.body: Presets recorded their duty by name and, when that name no longer matched, silently fell back to the first duty in the category - so a patch that renamed your duty could put up a listing for something else entirely. Presets now store the duty's id, which patches don't change, and when a duty genuinely can't be identified the listing is left with no duty set instead of guessing. Existing presets are upgraded automatically on first load.

changes.title: The window header shows the plugin version
changes.body: The line under the title now reads the running version instead of the preset count.

changes.title: Config schema v1
changes.body: Configuration.Migrate back-fills duty row ids for presets saved by earlier versions. Preset share codes are versioned behind a PFP1 magic prefix so the format can change later without breaking old codes silently.

releases.headline: Auto-adjusting locked job slots
releases.notes: Developed but never served from repo.json - its features reached users as part of 3.0.0.1.

changes.title: Auto-adjust locked job slots
changes.body: A toggle under the Auto Refresher. While you're recruiting as party leader, if a member leaves, any Party Finder slot locked to a single job is automatically widened to that job's role five seconds later - White Mage becomes regen healers, Red Mage becomes casters, Viper becomes melee - so the freed seat is easier to fill. If a slot is somehow locked to a non-combat job, it falls back to the standard auto-fill composition instead.

changes.title: A serious crash when duplicating or reordering presets
changes.body: Duplicating or reordering a preset from a card's menu could crash the plugin and, worse, corrupt the interface of Dalamud and every other plugin. Rendering is now hardened so a plugin error can never leak its styling into others.

changes.title: Taller preset cards
changes.body: Long descriptions are fully visible instead of being cut off.

changes.title: Ko-fi support button
changes.body: Added to the Applying Preset window next to the close button; the header button now reads 'Support me on Ko-Fi' with the heart.

releases.headline: Safety fixes and a delete confirmation

changes.title: Confirmation prompt before deleting a preset
changes.body: A misclick no longer wipes a preset instantly.

changes.title: A rare crash on unload mid-apply
changes.body: Could happen if the plugin was unloaded or updated while it was in the middle of applying a preset.

changes.title: Safer duty selection
changes.body: If a high-end duty has been renamed or removed by a game patch, the plugin leaves the listing's duty unset instead of posting a wrong one.

changes.title: Two options that never did anything
changes.body: 'Unselect Classes' and the item-level 'or Above' toggle were saved but never applied to the Party Finder.

changes.title: Codebase reorganised into Data / Game / UI
changes.body: No change to saved presets.

releases.headline: The Auto Refresher works end to end

changes.title: Auto Refresher performs the full Edit to Apply Changes sequence
changes.body: Matching the RecruitmentRefresher plugin's approach, so your Party Finder is reliably re-posted instead of just opening the window.

changes.title: Live countdown timer
changes.body: Sits next to the Auto Refresher toggle and shows the time until the next refresh. It starts once your Party Finder is up.

changes.title: Choice of refresh interval
changes.body: Every 15 or 30 minutes.

changes.title: /pfp refresh command
changes.body: Refreshes your listing on demand.

releases.headline: Party detection fixes and a redesigned status window

changes.title: Party job detection works when members are in different zones
changes.body: Auto-adjust slots read party jobs from the social party list instead of the in-zone party list, so a teammate being on another map no longer wipes out their detected job.

changes.title: Party leader detection updates when lead is passed to you
changes.body: The plugin could still think you weren't the leader after leadership was handed to you, blocking recruitment. It now reads the live party leader at the moment you apply a preset.

changes.title: The built-in Auto Refresher actually works
changes.body: Refreshes every 30 minutes using the same proven method as the RecruitmentRefresher plugin. The toggle sits as its own section above the Create button instead of overlapping it.

changes.title: Redesigned the Applying Preset window
changes.body: Matches the modern look of the rest of the plugin, with a friendly play-by-play and a smooth progress bar. Finishing shows 'All set, PF is up!' and a green Done button. The old settings-comparison list was removed.

changes.title: Assorted UI fixes
changes.body: Moved the Ko-fi button into the window header and made it bigger, surfaced the Auto Refresher toggle in the main window (hidden automatically if you have RecruitmentRefresher), fixed the Create New Preset button icon, and fixed long preset comments so they wrap instead of running under the Apply Preset button.

releases.headline: Private-party password moved out from behind the Apply button

changes.title: Password shown next to the preset name
changes.body: It's no longer hidden behind the Apply Preset button.

changes.title: Revamped design, usability and readability
changes.body: Reworked the look of the plugin throughout and fixed various bugs.

releases.headline: Applying a preset selects the right duty

changes.title: Presets no longer post as 'All'
changes.body: Applying a preset would often leave your listing set to All instead of the duty you saved, and you had to manually open the in-game duty menu once before presets would work. Applying a preset now sets the correct duty on its own.

releases.headline: Initial releases
releases.notes: Covers 1.0.5 and earlier; individual release dates were not recorded.

changes.title: Party Finder preset manager
changes.body: Save and manage Party Finder recruitment presets - duty, objective, roles, conditions, languages and more - and apply them with one click.
